name: Contentful
description: Contentful is an enterprise-grade headless CMS that stores structured content and delivers it via REST and GraphQL APIs. Content editors use the Contentful web app; developers fetch content in any framework. Strong for large teams needing workflow approvals, localization, and rich media management. The content model is flexible — define your own content types.

useCases.task: Fetch blog posts, marketing pages, or product content for a web app
Build a multi-language website with locale-specific content
Enable non-technical content editors to manage website content
Integrate structured content into a mobile app

setupSteps: Create a Contentful account at contentful.com
Create a new Space (a Space is your content repository)
Define your Content Types (the schema for your content)
Navigate to Settings → API Keys → Add API Key
Copy the Space ID and Content Delivery API access token
For write access, generate a Content Management API token under Settings → API Keys → Content Management Tokens
Set CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN, CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID, and CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID environment variables

pricing.freeTier: Free Community plan: 1 space, 25K API calls/month, 500MB assets, 2 roles, 5 users

rateLimits.limit: 25,000 API calls/month (Community), no per-second limit documented — burst throttling at 55 requests/second on Delivery API
rateLimits.notes: Content Delivery API responses are cached at Contentful's CDN globally. Cache invalidation happens on publish — unpublished content may be served from cache for up to 15 minutes.
rateLimits.retryStrategy: Implement retry with exponential backoff on 429 responses. Use the GraphQL API for complex queries to reduce call count (fetch multiple content types in one request).

codeExamples.title: Fetch blog posts from Contentful
codeExamples.notes: Replace 'blogPost' with your Contentful content type ID. The `include` parameter resolves linked entries (e.g., nested author fields) up to N levels deep. Avoid setting include too high — it increases response size significantly.

codeExamples.title: Fetch a single entry by ID
codeExamples.notes: Contentful image URLs are protocol-relative (start with //). Prefix with https: before using them in img tags or passing to image optimization tools. The body field for Rich Text must be rendered with @contentful/rich-text-html-renderer or @contentful/rich-text-react-renderer.

gotchas: Contentful's free plan has a hard cap of 25,000 API calls/month. A Next.js site that revalidates content frequently (ISR with low revalidation intervals) can easily exceed this. Always enable the CDN caching layer and set ISR revalidation to at least 60 seconds.

Rich Text content is stored in Contentful's own JSON format (not HTML or Markdown). To render it, you must use @contentful/rich-text-html-renderer or @contentful/rich-text-react-renderer. Trying to render the raw JSON as HTML will output [object Object].

The Content Management API (write access) and Content Delivery API (read access) use different tokens. The Management token has full write access — never expose it client-side or commit it to git. Use it server-side only.

Content models cannot be changed once they have content entries without migration scripts. Adding a new required field to an existing content type with 500 existing entries requires either a migration (run via @contentful/cli) or making the field optional.

reliability.notes: CDN-distributed with global edge caching. Content Delivery API responses are served from Fastly CDN nodes worldwide, providing low-latency reads for end users globally.

qualityJustification: Industry standard enterprise headless CMS with the most mature ecosystem and plugin library. Excellent content modeling, localization, and workflow features. Rich Text handling and steep pricing cliff ($0 → $300/month) are the main friction points for smaller projects.
bestFor: Enterprise and mid-size teams needing a robust headless CMS with content workflows, localization, and a rich editor for non-technical content managers
